newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile cobalt sales still on hold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile cobalt sales still on hold.

text.p: The sale of U.S. government stockpiled cobalt will remain on hold until further notice as the legal process continued, a Stockpile official said.
"We don't have a forecast as to when the next sale will be out yet," deputy Stockpile administrator Robert O'Brien said.
The Stockpile was asked last week by a Federal Claims Court judge for additional information about its sales policy.
The deadline for providing the information is April 18 and the judge was unlikely to reach a decision until after then, O'Brien said.

Minor Metals, a trading company, sought a restraining order on the March 31 sealed bid sale for 1 million pounds of cobalt because it was unhappy with the lack of "all or none" clause in the sales contracts.
The Stockpile wants the freedom to award just some of the metal requested by any bidder.
The March 31 sale was postponed until April 7 and then cancelled until further notice.
O'Brien said the lack of "all or none" clause applied to negotiated and sealed bid sales, therefore the next negotiated bid, which was due late April, is also now on hold.

The timing of the legal difficulties is unfortunate for the stockpile as cobalt prices have begun rising on the back of unrest in Zaire where the Lubumbashi head office of cobalt producer Gecamines has been shut.
